character: Silverstone's 2.64km National Circuit — the fast northern loop. Copse and the Maggotts-Becketts complex demand high-speed commitment, then a hard stop into the Brooklands-Luffield complex sets up the run to Woodcote. Rhythm through the fast stuff and a clean Luffield exit decide the lap.
sources: https://www.racingcircuits.info/europe/united-kingdom/silverstone.html ; https://oversteer48.com/silverstone-circuit-configurations/ — National Circuit (1.64mi/2.64km, 6 corners): Copse, Maggotts, Becketts, Brooklands, Luffield, Woodcote, using the Wellington and National Pits straights

corners.name: Copse
corners.technique: Requires commitment — only a small lift, smooth steering, trust the grip

corners.name: Maggotts
corners.type: fast left, first of the Maggotts-Becketts complex
corners.technique: Quick flick left, clip apex, immediately prepare for the right
corners.trap: Over-driving any part of this sequence ruins the whole complex

corners.name: Becketts
corners.type: fast right-left sequence (part of the complex)
corners.technique: Flow through with smooth, quick direction changes — carry as much speed as possible into the run to Brooklands
corners.trap: Fighting the car with big steering corrections; the section needs rhythm

corners.name: Brooklands
corners.type: medium-speed left-hander that tightens, heavy braking after the Wellington Straight
corners.technique: Hard braking in a straight line, late apex as it tightens, set up for Luffield
corners.trap: Braking too deep and missing the apex, compromising the Luffield entry

corners.name: Luffield
corners.technique: Long, tightening right — exit speed matters more than entry commitment; be patient on the throttle
corners.trap: Getting greedy on entry and running wide, killing exit speed to Woodcote

corners.name: Woodcote
corners.type: fast right kink onto the National Pits Straight (final corner)
corners.technique: Flat or near-flat in most cars — a clean Luffield exit carries all the way onto the straight
corners.trap: A poor Luffield exit means slow Woodcote and slow straight-line speed to Copse
